findings.F1: Inside the regime the effect is graded and on the predicted side, but only across the close's place in the day's range: next-day excess return by close-location quintile runs −0.79 % (t −1.54), −1.05 % (t −1.91), +0.14 %, +0.29 %, +1.09 % (t 1.51), about 308 cases each. The near-low tercile minus the near-high tercile is +1.72 % (Welch t 4.17, 511 vs 515 cases), against +0.54 % (t 3.61) outside the regime.
findings.F2: The main measure (t 1.30) clips the forecast at 0, so it can only use the near-low half of this gradient. The near-high half carries half of the spread. The bottom forecast tercile earns −0.94 % the next day (t −2.11, 513 cases) and the top tercile +0.95 % (t 1.74, 517 cases), so neither half alone clears t 2.
findings.F3: The effect is drowned by the regime's own noise rather than absent. The next-day excess return has a standard deviation of 6.93 % inside the regime against 5.24 % outside. A mean of about +0.4 % to +1 % per case therefore needs far more cases than the 1,188 independent days the test had.

ideas.name: near-low rebound, more coins
ideas.idea: When a coin's daily high-low ranges over the past 30 days are wide compared with the past 90 days and its 30-day return is negative, the lower its close sits within the day's high-low range, the larger its rise over the next 1 day, and the more so the deeper its 30-day fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy closes pinned near the day's low in agitated markets only while the coin is down over the month, and stay out of such closes in rising months, where the book's deepest falls occur.

ideas.idea: When a coin's daily high-low ranges over the past 30 days are wide compared with the past 90 days and its 30-day return is negative, the higher its close sits within the day's high-low range, the larger its fall over the next 1 day.
ideas.consequence: A trader would sell, or refuse to buy, closes pinned near the day's high in agitated falling months, since those bounces tend to give back the next day.
ideas.name: near-high close fades
